acme_ops: Hey team — since ~09:00 UTC we're seeing a lot of 429s and intermittent auth failures for our dedicated capacity tenant. Latency also spiked to 3-4s per token. This started after we rolled out longer prompts (12k tokens). Any ideas?

sam_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a sample request_id and a minimal repro payload? Also, are you seeing billing alerts?

acme_ops: request_id=req_0a7f9c22, one example curl below. Billing alert popped at 09:12 for "burst rate limit exceeded" but usage looked normal in the dashboard.

acme_ops: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-rlf-16k","input":"'$(python -c "print('A'*12000)")'","request_id":"req_0a7f9c22"}'
```

sam_support: got it. @leo_runtime @anya_sre assigning — looks like a Dedicated tenant issue (KV cache churn hypothesis).

leo_runtime: Looking at infra logs for tenant acme: I see frequent KV eviction messages around the same time: `kvcache: evict shard=4 size=3412275200 reason=fragmentation` and repeated `kvcache: reinsert failed - OOM soft limit` spikes. Also a stream of 429 throttle events mapping to the same machines.

anya_sre: Can you share the tenant allocation & autoscale config? My initial suspicion: many unique long prompts are hot-prefixing the KV cache, causing memory fragmentation and causing the allocator to trigger global eviction + throttle.

acme_ops: Autoscale config: min=2, max=8, scale_policy=cpu_based (scale up at 70% CPU). We didn't change autoscale. We do have a lot of distinct user prompts (personalized long context).

leo_runtime: That makes sense — autoscale by CPU won't react quickly to KV memory pressure. We also see slab compaction churn on those instances: `slab: compact start; freed=256MB; compaction_time=1200ms` which correlates with increased latency.

sam_support: Workarounds we can try immediately: 1) set max_context_tokens to 8k for the tenant (rate-limit long prompts), 2) enable prefix caching (sticky cache) to reduce unique KV entries, 3) temporarily increase Dedicated pool memory/instance count or adjust autoscale to include memory pressure.

anya_sre: For repro: please run a controlled script that creates many unique long-prefix requests to reproduce the churn. Example script: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"open-rlf-16k","input":"User:${i} '$(python -c "print('X'*11000)")'","request_id":"repro_'${i}'"}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```

leo_runtime: If you can run that and paste a sample timeline, we'll correlate with KV metrics. Key metrics: KV entries, eviction rate, slab fragmentation %, and per-shard allocation failures.

acme_ops: Running now — initial run produced 20% 429s within 60s. Attaching the snippet of the error we saw: `{"error":"Request rate limited: tenant_kv_eviction_throttle","code":429}`. Also saw intermittent `401: token verification failed` but token is valid; likely side-effect of auth service calls timing out.

sam_support: @billing-bot did any billing rule change trigger rate limits?

billing-bot: No manual billing rule changes for tenant acme. There was a short-lived automated "burst protection" alert fired at 09:12 due to sudden spike in token consumption; it auto-resolved at 09:18 after throttling.

anya_sre: Diagnosis plan: 1) reproduce with script and collect `kvcache.*` logs + per-instance /metrics, 2) temporarily switch tenant autoscale to memory-aware policy or increase min nodes, 3) deploy runtime patch that reduces aggressive slab compaction (we have a candidate config toggle), 4) long-term: add tenant-aware prefix caching and quota for unique prefixes.

leo_runtime: Immediate mitigation we can apply from infra side: bump min nodes from 2->4 for the tenant and toggle memory_pressure_scale=true. That should reduce realloc churn and buy time. Want to do that now?

acme_ops: Please do — we can accept brief cost increase. Also if you can whitelist the token so auth failures stop, that helps.

sam_support: On it. Applying min nodes bump and memory-aware scaling. Also temporarily whitelist token sk-acme-xxxx for auth retries. Will monitor.

leo_runtime: Changes applied at 09:37 UTC. Early signs: eviction rate down by ~60% on the affected shard and 429s dropping. Still seeing some compaction latencies, but amortized.

acme_ops: Confirmed — 429s are much lower and auth failures stopped. Thanks team!

sam_support: Follow-ups: we'll schedule a post-mortem and propose the config changes: add autoscale by memory, tenant-level prefix caching toggle, and a limit on unique long prompts. Also we'll surface best-practice doc to acme on chunking long contexts.

anya_sre: Assigning ticket to eng-runtime (ENG-5879) to evaluate allocator/tuning.

acme_ops: Appreciate the quick response. Please send the post-mortem when available. :thumbsup:
